added_sources.title: Bob Weyeneth and John Dichtl, “Update on the Journal,” NCPH, 1 May 2012.
added_sources.note: Institutional account read: UCSB launch in 1978 and continuing editorial home, university/society/publisher partnership. A participant account of institutional continuity; it is not a quantified content survey or evidence for global representativeness.

added_sources.title: Robert Kelley, “Public History: Its Origins, Nature, and Prospects,” The Public Historian 1(1) (1978), 16–28.
added_sources.note: Downloaded scan; read pp. 16–20, including externally posed questions, museums, government, preservation, consultancy and Kelley/Johnson’s 1975 training discussion. Later pages unread. His claims for policy benefits are advocacy, not independent evaluation; this is a US professional formulation, not the origin of all public historical practice.

added_sources.title: Social History of Medicine editors, “Chairs’ Choices Anniversary Virtual Issue” (2020).
added_sources.note: Read introduction and dated pre-2001 selections: journal began in 1988 after the Society’s Bulletin; articles span public health, clinical records and medical knowledge through 2000. Editors attribute choices to teaching, reception and personal experience. Later examples are not backdated; a commemorative selection is not a representative content census.

added_sources.title: Cambridge University Press, Urban History: 50th Anniversary Collection, selected pre-2001 extracts and abstracts.
added_sources.note: Read extracts of 1974 editorial, Reeder’s 1979 Dyos appreciation and Rodger’s 1992 retrospect; abstract of Lees (1994) and Lilley (2000). Publisher dates distinguish issue years from 2009 digitization. Full articles unread. Supports institutional continuity and varied approaches, not a uniform school or global census.

added_sources.note: Publisher lists Urban History Yearbook volumes 1 (1974)–18 (1991); Rodger’s volume 19 (1992) extract confirms the succeeding journal. Digitization dates are not publication origins.
